enonce_intro_markdown: The polynomial $f(x)$, where $f(x) = ax^3 - x^2 + bx + 6$, has a factor $(x+2)$. $f(x)$ leaves a remainder $10$ when divided by $(x+1)$. Find

questions.corrige_markdown:
By the factor theorem, $(x+2)$ is a factor of $f(x)$, so $f(-2) = 0$:

$$a(-8) - 4 + b(-2) + 6 = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; -8a - 2b + 2 = 0 \;\Longrightarrow\; 4a + b = 1.$$

By the remainder theorem, the remainder on division by $(x+1)$ is $f(-1) = 10$:

$$-a - 1 - b + 6 = 10 \;\Longrightarrow\; -a - b = 5 \;\Longrightarrow\; a + b = -5.$$

Subtract the second equation from the first: $3a = 6$, so $a = 2$. Then $b = -5 - 2 = -7$.

$$\boxed{a = 2, \qquad b = -7}$$

so $f(x) = 2x^3 - x^2 - 7x + 6$. Check: $f(-2) = -16 - 4 + 14 + 6 = 0$ and $f(-1) = -2 - 1 + 7 + 6 = 10$.

questions.enonce_markdown: the values of $x$ for which $f(x) = 0$. (8 marks for (a) and (b) together)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since $(x+2)$ is a factor, divide $2x^3 - x^2 - 7x + 6$ by $(x+2)$:

$$2x^3 - x^2 - 7x + 6 = (x+2)(2x^2 - 5x + 3).$$

(Check the expansion: $(x+2)(2x^2 - 5x + 3) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x + 4x^2 - 10x + 6 = 2x^3 - x^2 - 7x + 6$.)

Factorise the quadratic: $2x^2 - 5x + 3 = (2x-3)(x-1)$. Hence

$$f(x) = (x+2)(2x-3)(x-1) = 0.$$

$$\boxed{x = -2, \qquad x = 1, \qquad x = \tfrac32}$$
